title: 1987 AHSME Problem 10
statement: How many ordered triples \((a,b,c)\) of nonzero real numbers have the property that each number is the product of the other two?

solutions.text:
Multiplying \(a=bc,\ b=ca,\ c=ab\) gives \[ abc=(abc)^2. \] Since none of the variables is zero, \(abc=1.\) Also \(abc=a^2=b^2=c^2,\) so each variable is \(1\) or \(-1.\) Product \(1\) allows either no negative signs or exactly two, giving \(1+3=4\) ordered triples.

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: Translate the condition into \(a=bc,\ b=ca,\ c=ab\)
Multiply the equations and use the nonzero condition to determine the possible magnitudes
